topic: Endel Tulving (1972/2002): 'Mental Time Travel' — Patient K.C. Knowing Every Rule of Chess Without Remembering Playing a Single Game
visual_mode_reason: Endel Tulving's revolutionary 1972/2002 separation of **Semantic Memory** ('knowing facts about the world') from **Episodic Memory** ('autonoetic mental time travel into your own lived past *and* imagined future') — proven dramatically in Toronto patient Kent Cochrane ('K.C.'), who knew chess strategy, tire-changing facts, and family history yet had ZERO lived personal memories and went equally blank imagining next Saturday — is a pillar of hippocampal-default-mode neuroscience.

primary_case.title: Endel Tulving's 1972/2002 Episodic vs Semantic Dissociation & Longitudinal Study of Patient K.C. (Kent Cochrane)
primary_case.place: Rotman Research Institute (Baycrest) & University of Toronto

people.name: Endel Tulving
people.role: Estonian-born Canadian cognitive neuroscientist who split declarative memory into Episodic ('remembering') vs Semantic ('knowing') in 1972 and coined 'Mental Time Travel' / 'Autonoetic Consciousness'

people.name: Kent Cochrane ('Patient K.C.', 1951–2014)
people.role: 30-year-old Toronto engineering graduate whose 1981 motorcycle accident damaged bilateral hippocampi and frontoparietal cortex — leaving factual world knowledge intact while erasing EVERY single lived personal moment from birth onward.

people.name: Daniel L. Schacter & Donna Rose Addis
people.role: Harvard/Toronto neuroscientists who built on Tulving's Patient K.C. observation to prove the exact same hippocampal-Default Mode network constructs BOTH past memories AND future imagination.

core_facts.fact: In **1972**, University of Toronto psychologist **Endel Tulving** proposed a bold split inside conscious declarative memory that many doubted at first: **Semantic Memory** (timeless encyclopedia facts: *'Paris is the capital of France; bishops move diagonally'*) versus **Episodic Memory** (**'Mental Time Travel'** — stepping back inside a specific moment you personally lived: *'The rainy Tuesday in Paris when we dropped our baguette'*).

Nature delivered astonishing living proof in Toronto: in 1981, 30-year-old **Kent Cochrane ('Patient K.C.')** suffered severe head trauma in a motorcycle crash that destroyed his **bilateral hippocampi** alongside parahippocampal and medial frontoparietal lesions.

Ask Patient K.C. **Semantic** facts and he was sharp, polite, and articulate: he knew math, geography, vocabulary, **every rule and tactical opening of chess**, the **exact step-by-step procedure to change a flat car tire**, his own home address, and that his parents owned a summer cottage (he could point it out on a map of Ontario!).

Now ask Patient K.C. ONE **Episodic** question: ***'Can you remember a single game of chess you ever played? A single time you changed a flat tire? Even ONE specific afternoon from your entire life — even your brother's tragic death?'*** K.C.'s answer across **30+ years of testing**: **ZERO** — despite *knowing factually* that his brother had died, he could not re-experience a single personal scene from birth to the present.

Even more astonishing: K.C. could **learn brand-new Semantic facts** slowly over trials (definitions of new technical words, 3-word sentences via errorless learning) despite having **0% Episodic memory** of any study session.

Then Endel Tulving asked K.C. a question nobody had ever thought to ask an amnesic patient (**1985 / 2002**, SRC1): ***'Kent, what are you going to do tomorrow?'*** K.C. paused for 15 seconds and described his mental screen as **'completely blank — like walking into an empty room looking for a chair and there's nothing there — the exact same kind of blankness as trying to remember yesterday!'**

That single bedside conversation uncovered **why evolution invented Episodic Memory in the first place** (Schacter, Addis & Hassabis 2007 *Science*, SRC3): your hippocampus doesn't keep past episodes just for nostalgia — it **recombines past building blocks to simulate FUTURE scenarios**. Scan healthy brains remembering last summer vs imagining next summer, and the **exact same Hippocampal + Default Mode core network** lights up.

Pediatric corroboration (**Vargha-Khadem et al., 1997**): children with selective bilateral hippocampal injury at birth ('Beth', 'Jon', 'Kate') grew up completing **mainstream school**, learning reading, history, and factual science (**Semantic Memory intact!**) while forgetting every conversation and birthday party from ten minutes earlier (**Episodic Memory gone!**).

wow_facts.fact: Sit across a chessboard from **Patient K.C.** in Toronto: he plays a smart tactical game, explains castling and forks clearly — and **cannot remember a single chess game he has ever played in his entire 62-year life**, including the one five minutes ago.
wow_facts.why_surprising: 'Knowing the world' (Semantic) vs 'Reliving your life' (Episodic) split cleanly in two.

wow_facts.fact: Ask K.C. *'What happened yesterday?'* — **Blank.** Ask *'What might you do tomorrow afternoon?'* — **The EXACT SAME BLANK!** Without episodic memory of the past, the human mind loses its ability to **time-travel into the future**.
wow_facts.why_surprising: Memory isn't built for yesterday; it is built to simulate tomorrow.

wow_facts.fact: Children born with damaged hippocampi (Vargha-Khadem 1997) still passed school geography, vocabulary, and science exams via intact cortical **Semantic Memory** — while forgetting what happened at recess every single day.
wow_facts.why_surprising: You can learn encyclopedias of facts without recording a single personal episode.

wow_facts.fact: Tulving called Episodic Memory *'the only discovery in science that directly defies the physical arrow of time'* — letting a human sitting in a chair in 2026 travel backward 20 years and forward 20 years inside five seconds.

misconceptions.myth: Factual textbook knowledge ('Semantic') and personal life memories ('Episodic') sit in the exact same memory bank.
misconceptions.truth: Patient K.C. and developmental-amnesia children proved cortical semantic knowledge can remain rich (and even grow via errorless learning) when bilateral hippocampal injury wipes episodic reliving to zero.

misconceptions.myth: Memory exists strictly to keep an accurate archive of the past like a security camera.
misconceptions.truth: Tulving and Schacter proved episodic memory is **constructive Mental Time Travel** — built flexible so we can remix past pieces to preview **future** choices before taking real-world risks.

misconceptions.myth: Imagining the future uses pure 'creative frontal lobes' with zero involvement of the hippocampus.
misconceptions.truth: 2007 *Science* / *PNAS* studies proved hippocampal patients imagine shockingly barren, empty future scenes, and healthy fMRI lights up the hippocampus just as strongly for **+5 years in the future** as **-5 years in the past**.

everyday_hooks: Knowing 100% that the capital of Japan is Tokyo (**Semantic 'Know'**) with zero memory of the 4th-grade afternoon you learned it — versus instantly smelling the campfire from your 16th birthday (**Episodic 'Remember'**).
Planning an upcoming vacation or job interview by 'pre-living' walking into the room — literally running your hippocampal Mental Time Machine in forward mechanical relay dial.
Seeing why journaling 2 sensory details a day ('One-Line Time Capsule') rescues lived personal episodes from blurring into generic semantic summaries.
